_readme: Machine-readable headline figures from jslet. Each entry states the exact condition it holds under; none of these numbers is meaningful without its condition. Method, sources and exclusions: https://www.jslet.com/methodology
license_note: Facts are free to cite. Attribution optional.

numbers.condition: 10,000 requests per second, 1 KB payload, traffic crossing AZ boundaries

vendor memory labels are binary sizes: a card sold as "80 GB" holds 80 GiB = 85,899,345,920 bytes, reported by nvidia-smi as 81,920 MiB; weights and KV cache are computed in decimal GB, so the label is multiplied by 2^30/10^9 before any comparison
70B class: 80 layers, 8 KV heads (GQA), head_dim 128, 8K context, batch 1, FP16 KV
numbers.formula: 2 x 80 x 8 x 128 x 2 bytes x 8000 tokens

numbers.metric: KV cache size without grouped-query attention
numbers.condition: same 80 layers at 64 query heads, 8K context, batch 1, FP16 KV
numbers.formula: 2 x 80 x 64 x 128 x 2 bytes x 8000 tokens

numbers.condition: 8 KV heads versus 64 query heads at otherwise identical shape and precision

numbers.metric: KV cache size at long context
numbers.condition: 70B class: 80 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, 128K context, batch 1, FP16 KV

numbers.value: KV precision is independent of weight quantization
numbers.condition: quantizing weights to INT4 leaves the KV cache at FP16 in essentially every serving stack; assuming a 4x smaller cache understates it by 4x
70B parameters at FP16 (2 bytes per parameter)
70B parameters at INT4 (0.5 bytes per parameter)
405B parameters at FP16
671B-parameter MoE at FP16; all experts must be resident although only 37B are active per token
N-way tensor parallelism; more replicas of a smaller group beat one large group
RTX 4090 (1008 GB/s), 70B dense at INT4, one token requires reading every active parameter once
one A100 80GB, whether or not a single request arrives

numbers.metric: hosted API cost for the same traffic
numbers.condition: 70B-class traffic equal to the self-hosted comparison case
numbers.source: jslet model; vendor API list pricing

numbers.metric: share of total cloud infrastructure spend
numbers.condition: median mid-market SaaS at scale

numbers.metric: budgeted versus first invoiced monthly cost
numbers.condition: budget derived from the vendor pricing calculator; the gap comes from cardinality, retention tiers and log indexing rather than ingest volume

numbers.value: daily data created must be smaller than daily transfer capacity
numbers.condition: a migration is finite only while daily change (D x c) stays below daily capacity C; at or above a ratio of 1.0 the catch-up rounds grow instead of shrinking and no amount of retrying converges
100 TB, 1 Gbps, HTTP 12% overhead, 1 stream, 8-hour nightly window, 1% daily change rate

numbers.metric: effect of halving the transfer window
numbers.condition: daily capacity falls in proportion to the window while the calendar over which new data accrues rises in inverse proportion, so the convergence ratio scales as the inverse square of the window; halving the window multiplies it by four
the month length every major cloud pricing calculator assumes, defined as (365 days x 24 hours) / 12 months; an annual average that no actual calendar month matches

numbers.metric: spread between the shortest and longest month
numbers.condition: 744 hours in a 31-day month against 672 hours in a 28-day February, for a continuously running instance; the full range of monthly hour counts in a non-leap year
365 days x 24 hours, which equals 12 x 730; the identity that makes the 730-hour monthly convention exactly right over a year and wrong in every individual month

99.9% over a 30-day (720-hour) month, the basis published cloud SLA tables state; the same target allows 44.64 minutes in a 31-day month and 40.32 minutes in a 28-day month, and 8.76 hours across a year

numbers.metric: cost of moving 100 TB by direction
numbers.condition: AWS internet egress of 100 TB (decimal, 100,000 GB) on the cumulative monthly tier ladder; the same 100 TB inbound to AWS is billed at $0.00/GB
100 TB, 1 Gbps, HTTP overhead, 14-day dual-write at 1% daily change, 8-hour cutover outage at $5,000 per hour of business loss; total TCO $49,844

numbers.metric: Snowball Edge job-fee step at the 100 TB threshold
numbers.condition: AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized (210 TB): $1,800 per job for up to 100 TB of load, $3,200 for 101-210 TB; effective $0.018/GB at 100 TB against $0.032/GB at 101 TB

numbers.metric: effective AWS egress rate at 100 TB of monthly volume
numbers.condition: cumulative monthly account egress of 100,000 GB; the marginal rate at that volume is $0.07/GB, not the $0.09 headline

numbers.metric: Direct Connect cost for 100 TB against internet egress
numbers.condition: 100 TB plus 14 TB delta at a 1 Gbps dedicated port: $0.02/GB data transfer out plus 800 billed port hours at $0.30/hr; 71% below the internet egress path for the same bytes

numbers.metric: fixed per-key overhead in Redis before the key name or value is counted
numbers.condition: 64-bit Redis 7 with 64-bit pointers: keyspace dictEntry 24 B (key pointer, value pointer, chain link) + value redisObject 16 B + key SDS header and terminator 4 B + value SDS header and terminator 4 B; an additional ~8 B per key is amortised from the hash-table bucket array
numbers.source: Redis source (dictEntry, redisObject, SDS) + jslet model

numbers.metric: Redis RAM for 1 GB of application data by key granularity
numbers.unit: GB at 100-byte values vs 1.08 GB at 1 KB and 1.00 GB at 100 KB
numbers.condition: 1 GB (decimal) of data stored as 10,000,000 100-byte values (+68%), 1,000,000 1 KB values (+8%), or 10,000 100 KB values (+0.1%); per-entry figures ~168 B, ~1,080 B, ~100,072 B after allocator rounding

numbers.metric: memory for 100,001 cached objects as flat string keys vs packed into hashes
numbers.unit: MB as string keys vs 1.7 MB packed into 100-field hashes
numbers.condition: 100,001 keys shaped object:102393 with short values, from Redis's memory-optimisation documentation: ~115 B per object one-key-each (~1,001 hash keys, ~18 B per object when packed 100 fields to a hash)

numbers.unit: fields (128 is zset-max-listpack-entries, not the hash default)
numbers.condition: Redis 7.0 and later; the Redis 6.2 and earlier ziplist spelling also defaults to 512. The 128 widely quoted is the sorted-set default, listed directly below the hash setting in the same redis.conf block

numbers.metric: internal fragmentation from jemalloc size-class rounding at Redis key scale
numbers.condition: jemalloc small-object ladder 8, 16, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 112, 128, 160, 192, 224, 256, 320, 384, 448, 512 bytes and upward; a 100-byte request is served from the 112-byte class and a 200-byte request from the 224-byte class, and a Redis key is four to five separate allocations

numbers.metric: weighted average annual PUE of the largest data centre each respondent owns or operates
numbers.unit: ratio (total facility energy / IT equipment energy)
numbers.condition: Uptime Institute Global Data Center Survey 2025, n = 681 respondents; the headline figure has been virtually unchanged for six consecutive years, with the 2020-2025 range spanning 1.54 to 1.59
numbers.formula: total facility energy / IT equipment energy over a year
numbers.source: Uptime Institute Global Data Center Survey 2025

numbers.condition: Google global fleet of large-scale data centres, trailing twelve months, all overhead included, 2025; Google states its overhead energy of 0.09 against an industry average of 0.54 is 83% less overhead energy per unit of IT load
numbers.formula: total facility energy / IT equipment energy, trailing twelve months

numbers.metric: share of the power bill that buys no computing at the industry average PUE
numbers.condition: PUE 1.54 (the 2025 industry weighted average); overhead share is 1 minus the reciprocal of PUE, so the remaining 64.9% reaches the IT equipment
numbers.source: arithmetic on the Uptime Institute 2025 average

numbers.metric: PUE of a hall designed to 1.50 at full load, measured at 20% occupancy
numbers.condition: hall provisioned for 5,000 kW of IT load with a 300 kW fixed overhead floor and a load-tracking overhead coefficient of 0.44; at 20% occupancy facility draw is 1,740 kW against 7,500 kW at full load, so absolute energy falls 77% while the ratio rises 16%; at 40% occupancy the reading is 1.59, above the 2025 industry average of 1.54
numbers.source: jslet model on the overhead decomposition in Springer, Energy and Sustainability ch. 9

numbers.metric: gap between average PUE and marginal PUE at 20% occupancy
numbers.condition: same model as pue-part-load-drift; marginal PUE is 1 plus the load-tracking coefficient, so 1.44, against an average of 1.74; pricing incremental load at the average overstates its incremental energy by about 21%

numbers.metric: U.S. industrial average retail electricity price
numbers.condition: United States, industrial end-use sector, calendar year 2025 annual average, nominal, energy component only, tax and demand charges excluded; the commercial equivalent is 13.41 cents and the all-sector average 13.63 cents
numbers.formula: annual average of monthly state-level industrial retail prices
numbers.source: U.S. EIA Electric Power Monthly, Table 5.3

numbers.metric: PUE spread introduced by the choice of IT metering point
numbers.condition: same building; moving the whole electrical-loss band (14% of IT load) across the PUE fraction reads 1.49 when the losses count as facility overhead and 1.35 when they count as IT; for scale, the Uptime weighted average improved only 0.11 between 2014 (1.65) and 2025 (1.54)
numbers.source: jslet model on the Springer decomposition and the Uptime Institute series

numbers.condition: positive leap seconds inserted between the 1972-01-01 offset and 2026; the most recent at 2016-12-31; no leap second scheduled at the end of December 2026
numbers.source: IERS Bulletin C 72 (6 July 2026); NIST Leap Seconds FAQs

numbers.condition: in force from 2017-01-01 until further notice; UTC-TAI = -37 s
GPS time = TAI - 19 s and TAI - UTC = 37 s, so GPS leads UTC by 18 s as of 2026
numbers.source: NTPsec rollover documentation; IERS Bulletin C 72

numbers.condition: signed 32-bit time_t, epoch 1970-01-01; equals 2038-01-19 03:14:07 UTC; the next second wraps to 1901-12-13 20:45:52 UTC
numbers.source: POSIX / platform documentation; APNIC rollover table

numbers.condition: NTP epoch 1900-01-01; the field fills at 2036-02-07 06:28:16 UTC and rolls from era 0 to era 1
numbers.source: NTPsec rollover documentation; APNIC rollover table

numbers.metric: serial number of the Unix epoch
numbers.condition: 1900 date system; the 1904 date system is exactly 1462 days apart and gives 24107 for the same instant; serial 60 is the non-existent 1900-02-29
epoch 1601-01-01, the first year of the four-hundred-year Gregorian cycle active when Windows NT was designed
numbers.source: Microsoft The Old New Thing; NTFS documentation

numbers.metric: fires in the annual-average month for * * * * *
numbers.condition: every-minute expression, month defined as 365/12 days = 730 hours = 43,800 minutes

numbers.metric: difference between the annual-average month and a flat 30-day month
numbers.condition: every-minute expression; 43,800 minutes vs 43,200 minutes
minute field step of 7, selecting minutes 0,7,14,21,28,35,42,49,56
numbers.source: Vixie cron crontab(5), NOTES on field-local steps

numbers.condition: both day fields restricted, combined with OR per POSIX and Vixie; 2026 has 52 Fridays, 12 thirteenths and 3 dates that are both
numbers.source: POSIX.1-2024 crontab; Vixie cron crontab(5) note

numbers.condition: day-of-month 31; only seven months in a common year have a thirty-first day
numbers.source: calendar arithmetic; Vixie cron has no last-day token

numbers.condition: once-daily expression, annual-average month of 365/12 days
common year of 365 days; a leap year adds 1,440
